title: A trainer's weekly time budget and honest availability
audience: Personal trainers planning how many hours to offer clients while still finding new clients and running the business.
learningOutcomes: Build a weekly time budget that covers all seven categories of work, using hours drawn from a logged week
Publish availability that matches across every channel, and includes travel time for home visits
Refuse an unavailable time honestly, offer a real alternative or a referral, and record the action taken

instruction.heading: Your hours limit your income
instruction.body: A personal trainer's time is finite. Income from sessions depends on how many hours are available for training, and every other task competes with those hours. Planning starts by writing down the hours you work in a normal week, and deciding how many of them go to clients. Keeping that figure honest matters more than making the plan look full.

instruction.heading: The seven parts of a working week
instruction.body: A realistic week includes time for working with clients, managing client records and programmes, looking for new customers, preparing marketing and advertising materials, other business duties such as invoicing and accounts, your own exercise, and personal time and home life. Leave out any one of these and the plan will fail in practice. A plan that gives the whole week to clients leaves no time to find the next client, and no time to rest.

instruction.heading: Publish availability you can keep
instruction.body: Set the hours you are available, and publish them in the same form on your website, booking page and messages. Include travel time for home visits, so that a 45-minute session does not hide an hour of driving either side. Keep to the times you offer, because reliable hours build trust. Availability is not a device for creating scarcity. Describe the hours you really offer, and do not invent a shortage.

instruction.heading: When the schedule is full
instruction.body: If a prospect asks for a time you cannot offer, be direct. Offer a different time you truly have, suggest a later start if it suits them, or refer them to another trainer. Keep a record of any referral. A short, honest answer keeps a relationship that may lead to work later, and it protects the quality of the sessions you already run.

instruction.heading: Build the budget from a logged week
instruction.body: Plan from the hours you actually use, not the hours you hope to use. Log your time for one normal week, sorted into the same seven categories. Compare the log with the plan, and move hours until the plan balances. Repeat the log after about a month. Admin time is easy to underestimate, so the log is the check. The method for estimating admin hours in “Owner time and admin workload before the first job” can be used here.

procedure: Write the hours you can work in a normal week
Log one normal week in the seven categories
Set the hours you will offer clients, including travel time
Compare the log with the plan, and move hours until the plan balances
Publish the same availability on every channel
Record each refused time and the action taken, and log the week again after about a month

workedExamples.situation: Priya has a full-time corporate job of about 40 hours a week and wants to train clients before 6 am and after 5 pm. Her plan has 18 hours of client sessions a week.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Is the plan realistic, and what should she change?
workedExamples.reasoning: Eighteen session hours may fit, but the plan leaves out travel, admin, finding clients and marketing. She should log one normal week, add the missing categories, and reduce the session hours until the plan balances. She publishes only the hours she can keep, and refers any early enquiries she cannot fit.

workedExamples.situation: Dion has a full Saturday of home visits. A prospect asks for a 9 am Saturday start, which he does not offer.
workedExamples.reasoning: He should say that the time is not available, and offer a weekday time or a later Saturday start if that suits the prospect. If neither works, he refers the prospect to another trainer and records the referral. He does not mark the time as booked when it is not.

equipmentAndPpe: No PPE is needed for this lesson
A travel time record for home visits

commonErrors.prevention: Include prospecting, admin, marketing and personal time in the same plan.

commonErrors.error: Publishing hours that differ between channels
commonErrors.prevention: Keep one source for availability, and copy it to every channel.

commonErrors.error: Leaving travel time out of the schedule
commonErrors.prevention: Add the drive time before and after each home visit.

commonErrors.error: Creating an artificial shortage to push bookings
commonErrors.prevention: Describe only the hours you actually offer, and say so when they are full.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: See the relevant safety lessons for the site.

qualityStandard: The time budget lists all seven categories, with hours taken from a logged week
Published availability matches across every channel
Each refused time is recorded with the action taken: an alternative offered, a later start, or a referral
documentationEvidence: Weekly time log for one normal week
Time budget with the hours for each category
Dated availability statement with travel time noted
Referral record for each refused time
summary: A time budget must include prospecting, admin and marketing as well as sessions
Plan from logged hours, not from hopes
Publish availability you can keep, and include travel time
Refuse honestly, offer a real alternative or refer on, and record the action

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should a trainer's time budget cover prospecting and admin, and not only sessions?
options: Sessions alone leave no time for the work that finds and keeps clients
A regulator sets a fixed number of admin hours for every trainer in the country
Clients pay for sessions only, so admin is an extra cost

knowledgeChecks.question: A prospect asks for a time you do not offer. What is the honest response?
options: Say the hour is full when it is not to avoid a difficult talk
Say it is not available, and offer a real alternative or a referral
Offer it anyway and move other clients around at short notice

knowledgeChecks.question: What is the best basis for a time budget?
options: The hours a competitor says they work
The ideal week on a planning template
The hours recorded over real weeks
